articleTitle: Passive Intermodulation And Its Effect On Space Programs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: Many communication systems today transmit and receive several different closely spaced channels simultaneously through the same antenna path. Any interaction and mixing of these signals by passive devices in the signal path, can result in unwanted mixed signal passive intermodulation (PIM) products. If these PIM products are significant, and occur within the frequency band of the receiver, then the performance of the system in that receiver band will be affected. It is therefore of great importance to ensure that any PIM products which occur within a receiver band, are below the threshold of significance for that band. Communication systems are composed of many interconnecting components between the transmitter and the antenna and the antenna and the receiver. These components may take the form of waveguides, cables, filters, combiners and the antenna itself and its accessories. All of these devices need to be manufactured and connected together in such a manner, that the PIM products generated, are insignificant in the operating bands and at the transmitter power levels which are used. In order to achieve the performance required one must be able to reliably measure the PIM products of the components concerned, both singly and together, under different conditions and for different signal power levels and frequencies. To this end the IEC working group TC46 WG6 are working towards standardising test methods and understanding the processes involved in PIM-emissions, to meet the needs of the rapidly developing telecommunications market.

articleTitle: Screening of cables in the MHz to GHz frequency range extended application of a simple measuring method
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: Although cables are passive components, which can not disturb the circumference by its own, their electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is as important as the EMC of active devices, which are connected with those cables. The increasing use of cables, especially in the field of information technologies and cable distributed television systems up to very high frequencies requires new measuring methods for determination of the screening effectiveness of those cables. These methods shall be cheap, easy to use, applicable up to the GHz range and with good reproducibility. An investigation shows, that the well known triaxial measuring method with a one-sided short circuit commonly used for lower frequencies retains its merits also in the GHz range. The extension of this triaxial method up to higher frequencies was first investigated in 1993 in Germany. After two years of discussion and improvement in the international working group IEC TC46/WG5 it became a Committee Draft, IEC 46A/320/CDV, "shielded screening attenuation test method".

articleTitle: Passive intermodulation and its effect on space programs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: Intermodulation products are generated when multiple frequency signals are applied to a circuit element having a non-linear input/output characteristic. The space community first became aware of passive intermodulation (PIM) problems due to the difficulties encountered by the Fleetsatcom program. The concern with PIM remains today. Following a discussion of how past and present space programs concerned with PIM resolved the difficulties this paper provides a guide for selection of materials, typical PIM test set and facility designs including the design of a thermal enclosure to perform PIM test at temperature extremes. The paper concludes with a description of some facilities capable of performing PIM measurements on large reflector assemblies and complete satellites.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: The frequency range of balanced pairs or quads, e.g. for horizontal floor wiring for data communication has increased up to the GHz range. Especially in this field of data transmission a high screening effectiveness and a good EMC behaviour of such cables is required. In order to measure the EMC-behaviour of these cables, new measuring procedures have been developed which are under discussion for international standardisation. The screening effectiveness of screened balanced pairs is the sum of the unbalance attenuation of the pair and the screening attenuation of its screen which is described as the coupling attenuation. With the new triaxial measuring procedure and its measuring tube in accordance to IEC 46A/320/CDV the screening attenuation of the screen and the coupling attenuation of the complete cable can be measured. The difference of the coupling attenuation and the screening attenuation is the unbalance attenuation. In this way the unbalance attenuation of balanced cables may be measured up to the GHz range with baluns without a centre tap.

articleTitle: Improvement of the absorbing clamp coupling and screening attenuation measurements and standards for symmetric and coaxial cables and connecting hardware (connectors and cable assemblies)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: This paper describes developments in one of the test methods for screening, which is described in the IEC standard for radio-frequency cables, IEC 61196-1. The test method is an open site test for screening attenuation, which uses an absorbing clamp to pick up disturbing signals on the screen. During development work performed by a CENELEC working group, TC 46 X/WG 3, this method has been extended to measure the electromagnetic properties of symmetric cables (coupling attenuation), which is the combined attenuation of the disturbing signals due to screening and balance. In addition calibration of the set-up has been modified so that the complete calibration is based on measurements and not on calculations based on simplified theoretical models. The test method and performance limits for the different classes of cabling components and systems are now under introduction in the standardization committees with the purpose of having better control of the electromagnetic performance of cabling. This performance affects, in conjunction with the associated electronic equipment, the electromagnetic compliance performance of cabled communication systems.

articleTitle: Screening effectiveness measurements of waveguides and accessories
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: The currently used test methods for measuring the screening effectiveness of waveguides has been reviewed together with a proposed new method. Preliminary test results have been obtained using three methods which indicate that the proposed new technique may be applicable for waveguides after further detailed studies and trials. It is the ultimate purpose of this work to produce an international IEC standard for testing the screening effectiveness of waveguides and waveguide assemblies.

articleTitle: Field and laboratory measurements of the screening effectiveness of CATV networks and DAB signal levels
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: DAB test transmissions in Helsinki, started in February 1994 on 105 MHz, were transferred to the final frequency 220.35 MHz (block 11C) in March 1996. This resulted in thousands of complaints to the Finnish Broadcasting Company (YLE) and to the cable TV operator in the Helsinki area. The picture quality of the second national TV channel had suddenly deteriorated to an unacceptable level in these households. This was due to the on-the-air transmission of the DAB signal on the same frequency which was used for the distribution of this TV channel in the CATV network. The CATV operator has connections with an organisation of the private telecom companies in Finland. Most of its member companies operate and own CATV networks in the towns and cities where they are located. Several of them will face this same situation, when new transmitters in the Finnish DAB network start operation. This organisation set up a working group to investigate possible solutions to avoid the repetition of the interference problem. As a part of this investigation, Technobothnia Laboratory in Vaasa was asked to perform measurements which would give this group information on the state of the CATV networks in use and on the levels of the disturbing DAB signal.

articleTitle: Test fixture design and shielded screening attenuation performance of CATV coaxial cable
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: This paper describes a practical test fixture that has been developed for the measurement of shielded screening attenuation (shield effectiveness) of community antenna television (CATV) coaxial cable. The theoretical base of the fixture is contained in the draft Amendment 1 to International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) Standard 61196-1 and the original German development publications. The test fixture housing is a cylinder that forms a triaxial test configuration with the cable sample shield and centre conductor. The test fixture is thus composed of two regions; the test chamber and the cable sample. The test chamber diameter ratio determines the upper frequency test limit and the lower frequency limit is determined by the length of the cable sample. The sensitivity of the test method is limited by contact resistance where the cable sample shield forms a short circuit with the cylindrical test fixture end plate and by leakage from the cable sample termination which is located within the fixture test chamber. These factors have been minimised to achieve a measurement capability greater than 140 dB over the 1-1000 MHz frequency range. Test results are presented for a selection of braid and combination foil-braid shield designs for RG 6 type coaxial cable measured in lengths up to 6.7 meters over the frequency range 1-1000 MHz. The paper concludes that the test fixture is a satisfactory implementation of the shielded screening attenuation test method. However, recommendations are given for further study of combination foil-braid shield performance.

articleTitle: Measurement of coupled noise attenuation with special respect to frequencies below 30 MHz
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: After the initial problems affecting the transmission of data services at bit rates of 100+ Mbit/sec along twisted-pair (TP) cables had fully been solved through the introduction of state-of-the-art technologies for the production of cables, it became quite clear that-besides the parameters specific to the transmission technology-still other parameters had to be taken into account in order to be able to proceed from lab-type units to proven systems which are suitable for everyday operation by end users. In this connection, the so-called electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is of crucial importance for these systems. EMC means, on the one hand, that running systems do not disturb the function and/or operation of other devices and systems, and, on the other hand, that such systems are not disturbed either by the operation of different devices and systems. The article reviews how cable manufacturers, designers and end-users can exactly test the influence of cable technologies on the EMC characteristics of systems without, however, having to use a large number of measuring devices.

articleTitle: Measurements of screening effectiveness of multi-pin and coaxial connectors to 300 and 1000 MHz
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: The measurement of transfer impedance as a guide to the screening effectiveness of coaxial cables and connectors is well established, but only recently has a serious effort been made to extend the technique to multi-pin connectors used at frequencies up to 1 GHz. Among the many connectors in common use, the D-connector is one family whose widespread use keeps them inexpensive. If only for this reason this paper is written round testing of D-connectors, though its conclusions are applicable to most ranges of multi-pin connectors used in the digital instrument industry. Quite apart from the cost of components to be tested, if adequate screening is needed, it is important that the means of assessing this should not be costly. The test method described is being discussed and modified by a Working Group of IEC Technical Committee 46 and, to cover the frequency range deemed necessary, uses test equipment which might be thought expensive, though the test itself is simple. An alternative test is also suggested which is easier to use but is limited to frequencies where the test sample is electrically small. It is particularly useful in investigating the fundamental problems of using such connectors at high frequencies without the need for special test jig. It can be carried out with commonly available and inexpensive laboratory equipment, and may be made in the time domain, with the diagnostic benefits this brings.

articleTitle: The screening of CATV cable assemblies: proposed test methods with results for frequencies from 0.1 MHz to 1 GHz
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: Because of the need for improved screening on TV connectors which are used widely for connecting a TV set to its antenna and video recorder, an IEC specification has been prepared which includes details of screening attenuation. The specification is not yet published but will have the title IEC 60966-2-4: Radio frequency and coaxial cable assemblies-Part 2-4: Detail specification for cable assemblies for radio and TV receivers. The screening attenuation specified has a maximum value of 75 dB up to 1 GHz and 55 dB up to 3 GHz. There is some argument as to how this should be derived for a cable assembly, so a way round the problem is given here, where the screening attenuation is derived from individual measurements of transfer impedance (Z/sub T/) on the connectors and cable of the cable assembly. It is also proposed that these measurements can usefully be carried out at frequencies below 100 MHz. Measuring methods, one for frequencies up to 1 GHz, and another limited to about 100 MHz, are first described. Their use is demonstrated with a variety of TV cable assemblies and connectors bought on the retail market. Finally an approximate way of converting the Z/sub T/ measurements to a/sub s/ (screening attenuation) values is used. It is of interest that only one of the cable assemblies tested showed any probability of meeting the limit of the IEC specification.

articleTitle: Background and introduction to EM screening (shielding) behaviours and measurements of coaxial and symmetrical cables, cable assemblies and connectors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: The theory and related parameters of screening (shielding) are identified and behaviour explained. The concepts of the square root of power waves, general coupling functions and operational attenuation are introduced. The coupling mechanisms between parallel lines are explained and the influence of cable (coupling) lengths and frequencies is outlined and a summing function envelope called screening attenuation introduced. Theoretical curves with different cable screening parameters are shown. The mechanism of the leakage of a single braid is explained and shows that a perforated tube cannot be used as a model for a braided screen. The advantages and shortcomings of 16 different test methods of screen have been stated. Some preliminary statements of the measurement of the coupling attenuation of balanced cables are made. It seems to be an agreement between screening specialists that ITU-T Recommendation G 117 [32 ITU-T] could be used as definitions and principal measurement set-ups for the symmetry to earth of balanced cable pairs also in the 100s of MHz transmission region. Since both screening attenuation and coupling attenuation are dependent on measurement set-ups the results have to be measured in standardised conditions or test results have to be reduced to standardised conditions. However, it is recommended that both series of test results are given to avoid misinterpretation. Also in near and far end unbalance attenuations the capacitive and inductive coupling add towards the near end and subtract towards the far end.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic screening and crosstalk of ICT access networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Screening Effectiveness Measurements (Ref. No. 1998/452)
abstract: There is an urgent need to continue the research in balanced access and data cables crosstalk and screening performance. Digital transmission and equipment design have made very high bit rates possible over copper pairs. Also the capacity of old existing cables have increased considerably because of the introduction of very advanced adaptive transmission techniques. When the crosstalk is under control, considerably reduced and compensated a limiting factor can be the immunity against external disturbances. An inexpensive and effective way to improve the immunity of cables is to provide the cable with a metallic overall screen and to reduce the size of the common mode earth loops in the installations.
